candidates.title: Inertial Fusion Energy Model - PROCESS (UKAEA)
candidates.notes: Page focuses on driver physics parameters (efficiency, target gain, driver energy) and geometric inputs. No capacity factor or plant availability model documented. IFE module sets up physics constraints only — economic/operational metrics not included.

candidates.title: Complexity And Availability for Fusion Power Plants: The Potential Advantages of Inertial Fusion Energy (Journal of Fusion Energy)
candidates.notes: 303 redirect — Springer institutional access required. Title is directly relevant to IFE availability modeling, but content not accessible.

candidates.title: A simplified economic model for inertial fusion (Hawker 2020, Royal Society/PMC)
candidates.notes: Full open-access paper. Treats availability as a free parameter (50–100%, default 70%). Explicitly notes no IFE-specific availability sub-model exists and proposes a parametric approach. Also contains O&M cost range ($10–100/kWe-yr from gas/nuclear analogues). Extracted — covers G-3 and G-9 partially.

entries.notes: No IFE-specific rep-rate-coupled availability model found in any accessible source. Hawker 2020 addresses availability parametrically (70% default, 50–100% range) with acknowledgment that a proper availability sub-model would require component failure rates. The Springer paper on IFE availability advantages is paywalled and is the strongest candidate if institutional access is available.

candidates.notes: Press release only. Describes GEM capabilities but provides no quantitative data. Actual model requires download from LLNL software licensing portal.

candidates.title: COST-EFFECTIVE TARGET FABRICATION FOR INERTIAL FUSION ENERGY (Goodin et al., 2004, OSTI)
candidates.notes: OSTI conference record of the Goodin 2004 paper cited in analysis. Has abstract showing: NIF targets ~$2,500 each; IFE direct-drive target achievable at $0.16/target NOAK; factory supply ~500,000 targets/day. Full text may require OSTI portal access.

candidates.title: IFE Target Fabrication, Delivery, and Cost Estimates (Goodin, Fusion Power Associates 2007)
candidates.notes: Direct PDF, accessible. 2007 Fusion Power Associates presentation by same author as the 2004 reference. Contains updated target fabrication and cost methodology. Extracted.

entries.notes: Goodin 2007 FPA presentation is the most accessible version of the Goodin target fabrication cost methodology. Contains cost structure, factory throughput requirements, and per-target cost analysis at IFE-relevant production rates. The 2004 OSTI conference record (biblio/828518) was not extracted as the 2007 version is more recent and accessible. GEM Excel model itself is not publicly available without LLNL license.

candidates.title: A simplified economic model for inertial fusion (Hawker 2020, Royal Society/PMC)
candidates.notes: Full open-access paper. O&M treated as C_O&M = ε × P_e, with ε in $/kWe-yr range $10–100 (from gas/nuclear analogues). No IFE-specific itemized breakdown. Covers G-9 partially. Already extracted for G-3.

candidates.title: Extension of the Fusion Power Plant Costing Standard (arXiv, 2026)
candidates.notes: Not triaged with WebFetch due to budget constraints. ArXiv paper from 2026 on fusion costing standards may include IFE O&M structure. Candidate for future iteration.

entries.notes: G-9 is partially covered by the Hawker PMC paper (extracted under G-3). That paper provides the only published parametric O&M treatment for IFE, using $10–100/kWe-yr from nuclear analogues. The arXiv costing standard paper (2602.19389) was not triaged due to search budget exhaustion and is a promising candidate for iter-3.

candidates.title: HYLIFE-II tritium management system (OSTI Technical Report, 1993)
candidates.notes: Abstract contains detailed cost breakdown: $92M total, 56% vacuum disengagers, 15% blast chamber vacuum, 9% cryogenic plant, 6% each emergency air cleanup and waste treatment, 3% protium removal, 2% each fuel storage and inert gas. Also gives FLiBe pumping power for tritium extraction: 6.6 MW. Extracted.

candidates.title: HYLIFE-II: A molten-salt inertial fusion energy power plant design — final report (OSTI, 1994)
candidates.notes: Full HYLIFE-II plant design report with economics. Not extracted due to budget limits; candidate for iter-3 to capture full plant capital cost breakdown.

candidates.title: Tritium extraction from FLiBe blankets using the CoRExt process (IFE-STAR project)
candidates.notes: Current IFE-STAR funded project for FLiBe tritium extraction R&D. Not triaged with WebFetch due to budget constraints. May be institutional page or project summary without capital cost data.

entries.notes: HYLIFE-II tritium management system report provides the only published cost breakdown for FLiBe-based tritium processing. The $92M figure and component allocation are directly usable for G-10. Note this is 1993 dollars and refers to HYLIFE-II architecture (heavy ion driven), not Xcimer's architecture — scaling and technology assumptions should be noted in analysis.

candidates.title: Criteria for the economic viability of fusion power plants (Whyte et al., 2026)
candidates.notes: Provides quantitative utilization factor model U = τ_op/(τ_op + τ_rep) applicable to all fusion concepts including IFE. Section 2.8 discusses IFE with flowing liquid wall as a use case. Framework mathematically couples availability/degradation to economic viability. No IFE-specific capacity factor values — requires concept-specific parameterization. Accessible HTML on arxiv.

candidates.title: OSIRIS and SOMBRERO Inertial Fusion Power Plant Designs, Volume 1: Executive Summary & Overview (1992)
candidates.notes: 1992 DOE design study for SOMBRERO (KrF laser IFE) and OSIRIS (heavy-ion IFE) power plants. Designs explicitly assessed for 'reliability and availability, economics, and technology development needs.' SOMBRERO is direct-line ancestor of Xcimer's KrF approach. Likely contains specific availability assumptions for a laser IFE plant. Full PDF accessible via OSTI purl.

candidates.title: OSIRIS and SOMBRERO IFE Power Plant Designs, Volume 2: Designs, Assessments, and Comparisons
candidates.notes: Vol. 2 of the same study — contains the detailed design assessments and comparisons including reliability/availability. PDF too large for WebFetch triage. Purl URL would be https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/836548 — extraction budget exhausted after extracting Vol. 1 and arxiv paper.

candidates.notes: Discusses RAMI (reliability, availability, maintainability, inspectability) qualitatively as a cost factor but contains no quantitative availability model or capacity factor values. High-level review paper.

entries.notes: Extracted two sources that address the gap from different angles: (1) Whyte et al. 2026 arxiv preprint provides a mathematical utilization/availability framework that applies to IFE concepts; (2) OSIRIS/SOMBRERO Vol. 1 (1992) is a full IFE plant design study that explicitly covers reliability and availability economics for a KrF laser plant (SOMBRERO) — likely contains the closest available analog to a rep-rate-coupled availability baseline. Highest-relevance inaccessible candidate: Springer paper 'Complexity and Availability for Fusion Power Plants: The Potential Advantages of Inertial Fusion Energy' (paywalled). Candidate for future iteration: OSTI 836548 (OSIRIS/SOMBRERO Vol. 2 — detailed designs and assessments) and OSTI 1841839 (Integrated Design for Robust IFE).
